competitor_patterns: Extreme depth wins: Bikerumor's #1-ranking piece is 24,890 words — nearly 6x our longest posts — with hands-on testing of 18 products, comparison tables, and a full FAQ. Google rewards exhaustive buyer guides in this category.

Freshness signals drive rankings: Every top-3 competitor explicitly timestamps their updates ('May 21, 2026', 'May 19, 2026') in both the title/H1 and the snippet. The year in the title is table stakes; an 'updated' note in the meta description signals recency to both crawlers and users.

Structured data trifecta: Top performers combine (1) a comparison table near the top, (2) an FAQ schema block, and (3) product review schema. Bikerumor and Cyclist both use all three; our pages with tables AND FAQ schema consistently have higher word counts and broader keyword coverage.

H2 structure mirrors buyer journey: Competitors organise H2s as named product picks (e.g. 'Oakley Sutro Lite', 'POC Devour') which capture long-tail '[product name] review 2026' queries as a side effect of their main guide — free keyword surface area we are not exploiting.

Meta descriptions are click-bait, not descriptions: Top CTR snippets lead with a concrete number ('We tested 18 of the best') or a direct benefit ('Protect your eyes from wind, sun and grit') rather than generic brand copy. This directly addresses our low-CTR problem on 'best cycling sunglasses 2026' (1.7% CTR at position 7.8).
our_gaps: Critical word-count deficit on near-top pages: Our best-performing ranking pages sit at 3,000–4,000 words; the #1 competitor is 24,890 words. Even our 'tested and ranked' guides are 6x shorter than the category leader, leaving us unable to match topical authority signals.

Thin short-form posts dragging the cluster: 22 of our 41 indexed pages are under 1,400 words — including key targets like 'gravel-vs-road' (1,037 words) and 'photochromic' (1,104 words). These pages likely dilute internal PageRank and provide little incremental topical coverage.

FAQ schema coverage at only 33%: With 27 pages lacking FAQ schema, we are missing rich-result eligibility on the majority of our content. FAQ snippets visually expand our SERP footprint and directly improve CTR — critical given our 1.2–1.7% CTR problem on high-impression queries.

No named-product H2 strategy: Our H2s describe concepts ('Why lenses matter', 'The fog problem') rather than named products. Competitors capture 'Oakley Jawbreaker review', 'Tifosi Rail review', 'POC Devour 2026' as bonus long-tail traffic within single mega-guides; we have zero equivalent pages.

Comparison tables missing from 26 of 41 pages: Tables are a confirmed ranking signal in this category (Bikerumor, 220triathlon both use them). Pages without tables — including high-impression targets like 'are-expensive-cycling-glasses-worth-it' — are structurally weaker than competing results.
keyword_opportunities: 'cycling sunglasses under 100' / 'best cycling glasses under €100 2026' — 220triathlon ranks for budget-angle terms with 6,240-word guides; we have a thin 'cycling-glasses-under-150' post at 1,088 words that doesn't own this intent.

'interchangeable lens cycling sunglasses review' — Evil Eye ranks #1 for this exact term and it maps perfectly to our core VellutoPuro/VellutoVisione product advantage; our existing interchangeable-lens posts are too short (1,088–1,712 words) to compete.

'lightweight cycling sunglasses review 2026' — Our 25g frame is our single strongest differentiator vs Oakley, Smith, POC; no competitor owns 'lightest cycling glasses 2026' as a dedicated editorial angle. Our 'lightweight' post is only 1,160 words.

'cycling glasses for long rides comfort' — Trigearlab's buyer guide captures this intent; our 'cycling-glasses-fit-for-long-rides' post is 1,332 words vs their 9,680-word guide. Comfort + no pressure points + 25g is a natural long-ride narrative.

'best anti-fog cycling glasses 2026' — We have four anti-fog posts totalling ~4,500 words split across thin URLs, when a single consolidated 4,000+ word authoritative guide would outrank all of them and capture anti-fog FAQ rich results.
next_post_guidelines: Target minimum 4,500 words for any post competing on 'best cycling [X] 2026' queries. The word-count gap vs Bikerumor (24,890) cannot be closed overnight, but moving from 1,100 to 4,500+ words per post is achievable and statistically necessary to rank top 3 on these queries.

Add a comparison table in the first 800 words of every new post — place it immediately after the intro paragraph so Google can index it as a featured snippet candidate. The table should compare at least 5 products across 5 attributes (weight, lens system, anti-fog, price, trial period).

Structure H2s as named product picks for any 'best X' post: e.g. 'Velluto StradaPro — Best Lightweight Pick', 'Oakley Sutro Lite — Best Premium Option', 'Tifosi Rail — Best Budget Option'. This captures long-tail product-review queries as a side effect and mirrors what Google is rewarding at positions 1–3.

Every post must include a minimum 5-question FAQ schema block covering the most-searched variants of the target keyword — e.g. for 'best cycling sunglasses 2026': 'What are the lightest cycling sunglasses in 2026?', 'Are interchangeable lenses worth it for cycling?', 'What is the best Oakley alternative for cyclists?'. This directly addresses our 33% FAQ schema coverage gap.

Open every meta description with a concrete number or test claim: 'We tested 12 pairs over 800km — here's what won' or 'Lighter than Oakley, cheaper than Smith: 2026's best cycling glasses ranked.' This combats our 1.2–1.7% CTR problem on high-impression queries by matching the proven snippet format of Bikerumor and Cyclist.

Consolidate thin anti-fog posts: Instead of publishing another standalone anti-fog page, redirect effort into expanding 'cycling-glasses-anti-fog-ventilation-2026-velluto-stradapro' to 4,000+ words with a table and FAQ schema. Consolidation avoids keyword cannibalism across four near-identical URLs.

Lead every new post with the 30-day trial CTA in paragraph 2 (not buried at the bottom). GSC shows 'oakley alternatives' at position 6.1 with 232 impressions — users landing on that page are in high purchase-intent mode; the trial offer is our clearest conversion hook and should appear before the fold.

A table is a single HTML addition that signals structured content to Google and improves scannability for users.

Update the published date and add an 'Updated: July 2026' note to the H1 or immediately below it on all posts dated before June 2026. Competitor snippets showing 'May 21, 2026' outperform undated content for freshness-sensitive queries like 'best cycling sunglasses 2026'; Google surfaces the date in the snippet and users click newer results preferentially.
